title: JWT-authorized CLI session completion request
description: CLI session authorization MUST be performed by an active tenant membership with role owner, resolved from the verified issuer and subject; caller-supplied tenant ownership is forbidden. The verified issuer and subject MUST resolve to exactly one active tenant membership before CLI session access; zero or multiple active memberships MUST fail closed instead of selecting an arbitrary organization. The provider MUST revalidate the row-locked session's persisted requested scopes as a non-empty unique subset of the current allowlist before API-key creation; malformed, duplicate, empty, unsupported, or retired persisted scopes MUST fail closed. Session expiry MUST be evaluated after the session row lock is acquired, using a non-transaction-start persistence wall clock in the same transaction for authorization and polling; transaction-start timestamps and service-process clock comparisons are forbidden. Before inserting an API key or completing a CLI session, the provider MUST validate both the complete authorization response and the prospective completed-poll delivery response against their authorities using the row-locked membership and generated key data; validation failure MUST roll back without key insertion or session mutation. After acquiring every relevant blocking membership, session, tenant-quota, and referenced-key lock, the provider MUST re-evaluate session expiry with a non-transaction-start persistence wall clock immediately before authorization commit, replay response, plaintext delivery, or delivery-copy erasure; expiry MUST roll back without key insertion, session mutation, disclosure, or erasure. After response validation and any provisional API-key insertion, session completion, or delivery-copy erasure, the provider MUST re-evaluate session expiry with a non-transaction-start persistence wall clock immediately before COMMIT; expiry MUST roll back every provisional change and prevent response or plaintext disclosure. A check performed only before those writes is insufficient.
